text:
Sandpapergate: Australia Test captain Pat Cummins faces fresh scrutiny after Cameron Bancroft's explosive claims
Cameron Bancroft backed up Usman Khawaja's claims that the whole Australia team knew about the 2018 Sandpapergate, contradicting strong denials about it from Test captain Pat Cummins; Bancroft's lengthy statement added another twist to the ongoing scandal for Cricket Australia
Wednesday 18 November 2026 16:18, UK
Pat Cummins' handling of Australia's Sandpapergate has been called into question, following Cameron Bancroft's explosive statement about the 2018 scandal.
Bancroft issued a 4,000-word statement on Wednesday insisting "the whole team" knew about plans to use sandpaper to tamper with the ball during the Test series against South Africa, supporting claims made by former team-mate Usman Khawaja.
The statement contradicts comments by Cummins during an extraordinary 68-minute press conference last week, where he forcefully denied renewed ball-tampering allegations, with Australian cricket rocked by conflicting reports from that series.
Cummins' management said on Wednesday there was "nothing in the [Bancroft's] statement that hasn't been answered", while Bancroft revealed last week's press conference was the "the final straw" in him deciding to speak out.
"I think that [statement] puts Cummins in a very difficult position," former England captain Nasser Hussain told Sky Sports News. "It's often not the crime, it's the cover-up that gets you. Finally, it looks like the truth is coming out from within that dressing room.
"I wouldn't be surprised if others came out [to speak] - they may take sides, but it was brave of Cameron Bancroft to come out and do what he's done.
"He's [Cummins] got some explaining to do because he was so strong. I was surprised he was so strong in his denial of what Usman Khawaja wrote in that book about the sandpaper scandal.
"Bancroft said himself that he felt betrayed and angry and alone after that press conference. If you're going to make that press conference 68 minutes, you better make sure everything you say is 100 per cent spot on."
'Cummins will have to talk about this again'
Bancroft was banned alongside then captain Steve Smith and David Warner in 2018, while his statement in the Western Australian newspaper revealed that Cummins' press conference comments made him 'feel angry, betrayed and alone'.
Cummins said he didn't want to answer questions again about that series after last week's press conference, although may be pressured into discussing it again after the latest fresh statements from past team-mates.
"He will probably have to [speak again] as Australia captain!" former England international Matt Prior told TNT Sports.
"His agent has come out with a statement to say he answered everything the other day, but he hasn't really because there's now new information that has come from Bancroft - there are a lot of question marks.
"There are coaches that need to stand up and be counted. This has completely opened this whole thing up. At what point do Cricket Australia not just owe to the public and to us as fans, but to the individuals whose lives were changed? They've got a responsibility to find out the truth.
"As much as everyone wants it to die down, it has become a big thing and you can't just brush it under the carpet."
On the statement itself and how Bancroft described the dressing room, Prior added: "If you ask me my experience in dressing rooms and how it goes on, whatever your plan is, whether ball swing or orthodox or reverse, that's the conversation that happens - everyone gets around (the table).
"The bowling coach is involved. The coach is involved. The bowlers are involved. The captain is involved. It's a team decision. That's why anyone that has been involved in cricket has found it really difficult to believe that the bowlers didn't know and no-one else knew.
"That statement, for me, actually screams of honesty."
How would the media manager know and not the bowlers?!
Bancroft gave a damaging account of conversations he had held with Cummins, Mithcell Starc and Josh Hazlewood during that 2018 Test, including the timeline of when sandpaper was used.
Cummins and the bowlers released a statement in 2021 denying they knew anything about the illegal tactic, reiterated by the Test captain last week, although Bancroft said more players knew and their media manager strongly objected using sandpaper.
"He [Cummins] could hide behind semantics and whether he knew sandpaper was being taken on the field that particular day or that particular session, but he directly said no," Hussain added.
"If you read the West Australian article from Bancroft, he says the media manager walked out because she was so unhappy with what was being discussed in a team meeting.
"How does the media manager know what's going on but a bowling unit doesn't? It would be the first time a bowling unit does not know what is happening to a cricket ball."
Will more players speak out on Sandpapergate?
The day began with Cricket Australia pledging to create an open forum for individuals to give their accounts of what happened, but former England captain Alastair Cook said that forum had been rendered "irrelevant" by Bancroft's statement.
"When Khawaja first came out, the first thing a lot of people thought was 'he's just selling a book'," Cook told TNT Sports.
"This one (the Bancroft statement) is an open, honest letter on his own accord, with clearly no financial gain to him about his experience of his eight-and-a-half years, and that's what's made me sit up (and listen).
"He's opened his own forum, hasn't he?" Cook said. "He has done it himself and hasn't allowed any administrator to get in the way of his words.
"It's the level of detail he has gone into and the level of detail that has gone into this statement, it has blown everything open. We had Cricket Australia this morning saying they have an open forum of safe spaces, but that is now irrelevant.
"It's another person telling his side of the story, that backs up three other players. We've not heard the end of it. Over the next 24-48 hours, it's all coming out - there's no doubt about that."
What next for Australia?
Australia play England in a five-match T20I series, beginning on Saturday in Melbourne, before further matches in Carrara (November 24), Brisbane (November 27), Sydney (November 29) and Canberra (December 2).
The Test side are next in action against New Zealand in Perth from December 9-13, with further Sandpapergate headlines likely in the days and weeks leading up to that four-match series.

קמרון בנקרופט פרסם הצהרה מפורטת שבה טען כי כל שחקני נבחרת אוסטרליה ידעו על התוכנית לשייף את הכדור במהלך סדרת הטסטים מול דרום אפריקה ב-2018. דבריו סותרים את הכחשתו החד-משמעית של קפטן הנבחרת, פט קאמינס, במסיבת עיתונאים שנערכה לאחרונה.

ההצהרה עוררה סערה מחודשת בעולם הקריקט הבריטי והאוסטרלי, כאשר שחקני עבר ומקורבים קוראים לחקירה יסודית ולחשיפת האמת המלאה מצד גורמי הניהול בענף. בנקרופט ציין כי חש תסכול ובגידה בעקבות התנהלותו של קאמינס, מה שדחף אותו לפרסם את גרסתו המלאה לאירועים.
